newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Howard won't commit Canberra to job target.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Howard won't commit Canberra to job target.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard refused on Monday to commit the government to an unemployment target for the next four years.
"I am not going to commit this government to a quantitative target," Howard told parliament.
He said Employment Minister Amanda Vanstone's comments last month that unemployment might still be at 8.0 percent at the end of the century depended on certain assumptions.
"You know what those assumptions were? The continuation of your policies," he told opposition leader Kim Beazley.
"If your policies are continuing then there's every possibility that unemployment in this country won't fall," he said.
Howard earlier said the unemployment rate would come down over time as long as his conservative government could free up the labour market and run a faster rate of economic growth.
Unemployment was 8.5 percent in July and Howard repeated that the government's forecast of unemployment staying at that level on average through the fiscal year to June 1997 was cautious.
